page: Microsoft Azure M208ms_v2 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the MSv2 family, designed for memory-intensive workloads. It features 208 virtual CPUs mapped to 104 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware allocation is dedicated, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The server is equipped with a massive memory capacity of 5700.0 GB, providing approximately 27.4 GB of RAM per core. For storage, it includes 4194 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, while lacking any onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results reveal a distinct performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests falling into the bottom 25%. However, the massive core count enables top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, with read-only small and large block operations reaching top-tier status. Redis SET operations also perform in the top 10%, achieving 149.33 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is strong.

The primary tradeoff of the M208ms_v2 is its low single-threaded efficiency, making it less suitable for workloads dependent on high single-core clock speeds. Qualitatively, this instance represents a high-density resource profile where the cost is aligned with the massive memory footprint and high core count rather than single-core compute agility. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, massive data warehousing, and heavy multi-threaded processing tasks that can leverage its 5.7 TB of RAM and 208 vCPUs.
